categories.main_business_segments: MACOM operates as a single reportable segment focused on designing, developing, and manufacturing differentiated semiconductor products and solutions. Its primary lines of business serve three end markets: Industrial & Defense (I&D), Data Center, and Telecommunications (Telecom). The company offers a broad portfolio of thousands of standard and custom devices, including integrated circuits, multi-chip modules, diodes, amplifiers, switches, passive and active components, and RF and optical subsystems. These products are incorporated into larger electronic systems for applications such as radar, data centers, wireless infrastructure, medical systems, and satellite networks.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: MACOM leverages advanced analog and mixed-signal circuit design, compound semiconductor fabrication (including GaAs, GaN, InP, and specialized silicon), and advanced packaging and assembly. The company operates internal wafer fabrication facilities in the US and France, with additional assembly and test sites globally, and supplements capacity with external foundry and assembly partners. Proprietary process technologies, system-level integration, and expertise in high-frequency, high-power, and high-reliability environments are core to its production methods.
categories.primary_customers_markets: MACOM serves over 6,000 end customers, including OEMs, contract manufacturers, resellers, and distributors. Its key markets are: (1) Industrial & Defense (military and commercial radar, electronic warfare, secure communications, space, industrial, medical, and scientific applications), (2) Data Center (high-speed optical and photonic connectivity for AI, machine learning, and high-performance computing), and (3) Telecom (carrier infrastructure, 5G/6G, SATCOM, fiber networks, and broadband access). No single direct customer accounted for more than 10% of revenue in 2025, but two resellers each exceeded 10%.
categories.geographic_coverage: MACOM is headquartered in Lowell, Massachusetts, and operates facilities across North America, Europe, and Asia. In fiscal 2025, 56.3% of revenue came from customers outside the US, with China and the Asia Pacific region accounting for 28.4% and 11.5% of total sales, respectively. The company maintains a global sales and support presence, with major manufacturing and R&D sites in the US, France, Taiwan, and Ireland.
categories.supply_chain_position: MACOM operates primarily as a component and subsystem supplier, positioned upstream and midstream in the electronics supply chain. It manufactures semiconductor devices and modules that are integrated into customers' larger systems. The company employs a 'fab-lite' model, combining internal wafer fabrication and assembly with outsourced foundry and contract manufacturing partners, providing flexibility and access to diverse process technologies.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: MACOM's strategy centers on expanding its addressable markets and product portfolio, strengthening customer relationships, and capturing more design wins to increase market share. R&D priorities include developing innovative high-performance analog, RF, microwave, millimeter wave, and photonic products, advancing proprietary process and packaging technologies, and integrating acquired capabilities. The company invests heavily in R&D (25% of revenue in 2025) to address emerging needs in data center speeds, 5G/6G, SATCOM, and defense electronics.
categories.revenue_model: The company generates revenue primarily through the sale of semiconductor products, including standard and custom ICs, modules, and components, to OEMs, contract manufacturers, resellers, and distributors. Sales are made on a purchase order basis, with a significant portion (32.3% in 2025) through distributors. Revenue is recognized upon transfer of control of products to customers, with some variable consideration for returns and pricing programs.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: MACOM competes in highly competitive markets against both customers' internal design teams and major analog semiconductor suppliers. Key competitors include Analog Devices, Broadcom, Credo, Marvell, MaxLinear, Microchip, NXP, Qorvo, Semtech, Skyworks, and Sumitomo. Some competitors have greater scale and financial resources. MACOM differentiates itself through its broad technology portfolio, US-based Trusted Foundry status, and focus on high-performance, high-reliability applications.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: In fiscal 2025, MACOM reported $967.3 million in revenue, up 32.6% from $729.6 million in 2024, with strong growth in Data Center (48%), Telecom (41%), and I&D (19%) markets. Gross margin was 54.7%. The company had a net loss of $54.2 million in 2025, primarily due to a $193.1 million loss on extinguishment of debt, but generated $235.4 million in operating cash flow. As of October 2025, MACOM had $112.1 million in cash and $673.8 million in short-term investments.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: MACOM emphasizes high performance, quality, and reliability in its semiconductor solutions, targeting demanding applications in defense, data centers, and telecom. Its value proposition includes deep expertise in analog and mixed-signal design, proprietary compound semiconductor processes, advanced packaging, and system-level integration. The company’s US-based Trusted Foundry status, broad product portfolio, and ability to deliver both standard and custom solutions provide competitive differentiation, especially for customers with stringent security, performance, and supply chain requirements.
